assigned.title: Catalog metadata source port, and the surfaces still importing the fixture array
assigned.notes: Closes a control-plane gap as well as a code one. The port landed with no task covering it: PL-0104 declares only catalog-card.tsx, routes.ts and routes.test.ts, so apps/web/src/lib/catalog-source.ts, catalog-source-registry.ts, their tests and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md sat outside every declared surface - unreserved against a parallel writer, and outside any approval fingerprint. This task declares that surface and carries the three import migrations docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md lists as follow-ups. lib/catalog.ts and lib/demo-catalog.ts are reviewDependencies rather than allowedPaths: the port's wiring lives in them and an approval has to bind to it, but they are not this task's to rewrite. The e2e mode split that catalog.api.spec.ts needs once the fixtures stop reaching a production build is deliberately NOT here, because e2e/** belongs to PL-0701; until it lands, that spec fails in the harness's default production mode and .github/workflows/ci.yml says so at the job that runs it. DECLARATION GAP CLOSED: e2e/src/env.ts added to allowedPaths. It was edited this round and no task declared it as a write path -- it sat only in PL-0706's reviewDependencies, which is a READ-ONLY surface by contract, so the edit was a genuine contract violation and an approval on either task would have bound to a surface narrower than the diff. The edit is THIS task's, not PL-0706's: the rewritten CATALOG_AVAILABILITY commentary is entirely about the port and the import migrations named in this task's acceptance -- the title route now resolving through lib/catalog-source-registry.ts via resolveSynchronousCatalogMetadataSource so demo-title-details.ts classifies no environment, the four discovery surfaces refusing in the single catalog_source_not_configured vocabulary, and the deletion of readFixtureCatalogItems from catalog-source-registry.ts together with getHomeCatalog from lib/catalog.ts. Its only reference to the runtime witness is the unchanged phrase 'the same nominal witness the playback fixtures need', which was true before PL-0706's move and is true after it; nothing in this file names a class, a constructor or classifyRuntime. env.ts is deliberately LEFT in PL-0706's reviewDependencies rather than removed: WEB_MODE and MANAGES_SERVER decide that task's production-versus-development assertion, so its approval must keep fingerprinting this file even though it does not own it -- which is exactly what the two-surface split is for, and is not the same-task allowedPaths/reviewDependencies redundancy the validator warns on. Collision-checked: e2e/src/env.ts is prefix-disjoint from every allowedPaths entry of PL-0203 (claude-media), PL-AI-0005 (claude-lead) and PL-0706 (claude-security, whose e2e entries are e2e/tests/*.spec.ts and e2e/src/fixtures.ts), and PL-0104 shares this task's owner so cannot conflict. PL-0701 declares e2e/** but is BACKLOG and unowned, and already latently contains this task's apps/web paths and PL-0706's e2e specs, so nothing new is created there.
assigned.acceptance: Discovery reads a metadata port instead of importing a fixture array. catalog-source.ts states the source contract in the published vocabulary - a CatalogItem plus a nullable rights basis - and refuses a record whose basis is undeclared or contradicts its item, by named reason, rather than defaulting either to something permissive; catalog-source-registry.ts is the only module that knows both the port and an implementation, and resolves to not-configured outside the NonDeploymentEnvironment allowlist so the fixtures are unconstructible in a deployment rather than withheld from one; and every remaining surface reads the registry rather than the demoCatalog array - app/search/search.ts, app/title/demo-title-details.ts, and app/api/v1/catalog/home/route.ts, which awaits loadHomeCatalog and maps catalog_source_not_configured onto its own status instead of serving empty rails at 200. When the last surface has moved, the raw demoCatalog export survives only for tests that must be able to name the fixture set, so search and the title page stop being fixture-backed on a build where the home rails are not. docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md stays accurate about what the port still does not solve.

implementationBaseProvenance.reason: PL-0105's implementation predates its claim and is already in committed history, so an ordinary start would record a base that is false. The base was DERIVED, not chosen: git log --reverse over apps/web/src/lib/catalog-source.ts gives the first commit that introduced the port module itself, and this is that commit's parent. The port module is the correct probe because nothing older can have created it; probing a shared consumer would repeat the PL-0104 near-miss, where the oldest commit touching the declared surface was the repository's root commit carrying an unrelated fourteen-line scaffold. The commit window, both endpoints and the base commit's own surface touches are published for the reviewer to confirm that no earlier commit belongs to this implementation.

review.evidence: CHANGES_REQUESTED on rights-review even though the original composition-root blocker is closed: demo-title-details now names no catalog implementation and the registry alone constructs demoCatalogSource, while the opaque-reference documentation correctly reflects its move into provider-sdk. The remaining deployment guarantee inherits the unresolved PL-0706 authority defect because both catalog registry accessors accept a caller-selected nodeEnv and feed it to the public capability mint, allowing production code to request test and obtain the development catalog despite the acceptance claim that those fixtures are unconstructible in a deployment. CATALOG_SOURCE.md also still describes NonDeploymentEnvironment as a private-constructor private-field class even though it is now the shared branded value. Fix the shared mint authority, route these accessors through the corrected boundary without caller-authored runtime identity, and update that paragraph to the resulting mechanism. recommended.title: notFound() never reaches the wire: dead addresses answer 200
recommended.acceptance: An unknown title id and a malformed watch id each answer HTTP 404 rather than a skeleton served at 200, proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run rather than by a route calling notFound(). The cause is that a segment's loading file wraps that segment in Suspense, so React flushes the shell at 200 before the access-fallback error escapes the render and Next can set the status; the root loading file wraps every route in the application, so per-route fixes alone are insufficient. Any fix must keep the loading skeletons rather than deleting them to move a status code. DEPENDS ON PL-0103 because the title route is that task's declared write surface and it is currently in REVIEW; this is a lifecycle dependency, not a technical one.
